DECISION.explanation:
The candidate's proposed representation has a concrete, already-precedented integration path through the existing single authority root and does not require, imply, or resemble any of the four disqualifying risks.

1. No second authority root. docs/architecture/README.md states plainly that ADR-MPS-CONSTITUTIONAL-INVARIANTS.md is the sole source of architectural truth and that every other document in the index, including the candidate's own cited sources (ADR-24-25, ADR-24-21, AI-GOVERNANCE-AND-HUMAN-AUTHORITY-01.md), is a domain-scoped specialization frozen under it, none individually claiming constitutional/root authority. ADR-24-21 itself says so explicitly in its own text ('SHALL operationalize, and SHALL NOT redefine' the constitutional invariants). AI-GOVERNANCE-AND-HUMAN-AUTHORITY-01.md is expressly a 'FROZEN mapping, NOT a compliance claim' that names a gap but freezes no contract — it cannot and does not compete for root authority. There is no second document anywhere claiming to be a general Decision authority on its own.

2. No parallel governance path. Every mechanical piece the candidate's delta needs already exists inside the sanctioned mechanism set: ActorReference/AuthorityEvidenceArtifact (ADR-24-21, itself an operationalization of the constitutional layer), and the kernel's own authority-artifact registry in packages/mps-governance-runtime/src/authorityTypes.ts, which already lists 'decision' and 'approval' as recognized authority artifact types alongside 'decision_impact' under GOVERNANCE-22.9-I13. The candidate is asking to formalize and tighten an existing, already-integrated category, not stand up a new one outside GovernanceEngine/ActorReference/AuthorityEvidenceArtifact machinery.

3. No authority bypass. The proposal makes authority binding *more* strict (mandatory ActorReference/AuthorityEvidenceArtifact + timestamp) using the existing ACT-21-I10-style binding rule, and explicitly preserves — rather than erodes — the GENERATED != DECISION / observation-cannot-become-authority boundary that ADR-24-25 and GOVERNANCE-22.9-I13 already enforce. It does not describe any path for observation, retrieval, or AI-generated content to mint or mutate authority state outside the existing chain.

4. No new duplicate source of truth. Section 3 of ADR-MPS-CONSTITUTIONAL-INVARIANTS.md already demonstrates exactly this pattern in production — a kernel-owned, canonically-versioned, namespace-owned artifact family (mps-decision-governance / dg-*) frozen directly into the single root, with its own 'Rule of change' (Section 0: ADR + golden/property tests) as the sanctioned amendment mechanism. The candidate's proposal is structurally the same move: add or amend a section of the same document (or a package-scoped ADR frozen under it, as ADR-MPS-022 and ADR-MPS-CAS-STORAGE-BOUNDARY already are) to define a canonical Decision family. Far from creating a duplicate, its explicit stated purpose is to collapse the real, already-existing drift confirmed in the codebase (packages/mps-promotion/src/contracts/PromotionDecisionArtifact.ts, packages/mps-evolution/src/governance/PromotionDecisionArtifact.ts, packages/mps-governance/src/artifacts/GovernanceApprovalArtifact.ts, packages/mps-governance/src/contracts/ApprovalArtifact.ts) into one canonical ancestor — i.e. it is aimed at eliminating an existing duplicate-source-of-truth condition, not adding one.

Since the proposal is explicitly scoped as 'a semantic delta, not implemented here,' and every element of that delta maps onto an existing, already-integrated mechanism or an already-precedented amendment pattern within docs/architecture/ADR-MPS-CONSTITUTIONAL-INVARIANTS.md, the integration path runs through the existing single authority root. Verdict: CLEAR.

AUTHORITY.explanation:
Falsification attempted against all 7 classes and each fails to eliminate the candidate.

(1) WRONG_ABSTRACTION_LEVEL — rejected. "Scope of what an actor is permitted to do, with fail-closed rejection outside that scope" is squarely governance-level semantics, not an implementation detail; the platform's own frozen ADR family (ADR-24-21 through ADR-24-26) treats it at exactly this level, as a peer of Decision Truth and Capability Trust.

(2) MECHANISM_ONLY — rejected for the candidate itself (its definition is normative, not procedural), though this is where the live implementation actually lands: today's only *enforced* representation is a scattered role-string check (`req.authUser.role !== 'ADMIN'`) repeated across 36+ route files (e.g. server/routes/admin.routes.ts:56-388) plus a single per-event signed predicate (PromotionAttestationPredicate) for quarantine promotion. Neither is a durable, canonical "authority" object — both are HOW a specific check is done at a specific call site, not a governed WHAT.

(3) ALREADY_REPRESENTED — tested against three candidate representations and FAILS the lossless reuse test for all three (see lossless_reuse_test). Closest match, ADR-24-21's AuthorityEvidenceArtifact/TrustDomainArtifact/TrustAnchorArtifact/TrustDelegationArtifact, is explicitly logged by the platform's own operational proof registry as `"package_class": "RETIRED_CANDIDATE"`, `"module_role": "UNWIRED_ACTOR_TRUST_MODEL"`, `"proof_status": "UNPROVEN"` with `"proof_reason": "TEST_EXISTS_BUT_IS_NOT_EXECUTED"` (docs/architecture/architecture-authority-map.jsonc, entry id "mps-governance-actor-trust", ~lines 866-880), and its compliance rule ACT-21-I1 is a stub that unconditionally returns `passed: true` with `evidence: []` regardless of input (packages/mps-compliance/src/validators/ACT_21_I1.ts:8-16). Nothing outside its own package/tests constructs an ActorArtifact/AuthorityEvidenceArtifact. A server/routes/governance.routes.ts comment (lines ~213-215) confirms individual actor-level, non-repudiable authority ("Level 3") is "a separate architecture-convergence track, not started."

(4) SEMANTIC_DUPLICATE — rejected. Capability (ADR-24-26) explicitly disclaims this role: "Capability beskriver vad som kan göras, inte vem som får göra det" (docs/architecture/ADR-24-26-Capability-Trust-Connector.md:48), and CapabilityCertificationArtifact takes AuthorityEvidenceArtifact as an external reference (CAP-26-I12, same file line 163-164) rather than reimplementing authority — the platform's own design treats Capability and Authority as distinct. Decision (mps-decision-governance) governs lineage/content of a decision, not the actor's standing to make it. No overlapping candidate found.

(5) DERIVABLE — rejected. The live RBAC role assignment is mutable, overwritten state in the user/session store, not an append-only ledger; there is no reproducible way to reconstruct "what actor X was permitted to do, under what scope, granted by whom, at time T" after a role change. This is the opposite of the deterministic, replay-compatible reconstruction the platform requires elsewhere (e.g. C-05 replay determinism in ADR-MPS-CONSTITUTIONAL-INVARIANTS.md §7).

(6) NOT_TECHNOLOGY_INDEPENDENT — rejected. Actor permission-scope semantics are independent of any LLM, risk-model, or forecasting technology choice; nothing about Authority would disappear under such a swap.

(7) NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_GOVERNED — rejected. ADR-24-21 is referenced as a shared dependency by five sibling ADRs (24-22 Signature/Attestation, 24-24 Retention, 24-25 Execution Identity, 24-26 Capability Trust, and indirectly 24-19 Workflow) via AuthorityEvidenceArtifact, which is the classic signature of a concept needing its own lifecycle/identity rather than being folded as an attribute onto one specific artifact type.

Because none of the 7 falsification classes eliminates the candidate, and because the one existing design that matches it (ADR-24-21) is present only as an orphaned, unproven, unenforced schema — not a live governing source of truth — the candidate survives as CORE_SEMANTIC_SURVIVES / TRUE_GAP. Note this is a qualified gap: the *semantic design* for Authority already exists on paper (ADR-24-21 + packages/mps-governance/src/actors/*.ts) and is even absent from the current authority chain (docs/architecture/README.md lists neither ADR-24-21 nor any Actor/Trust/Authority document in its §1 "current normative" or §3 "active domain contracts" tables, and ADR-24-21's stated constitutional grounding, MIMER-20-I8 "Explicit Mutation Authority" in ADR-24-20-Constitution.md:96-97, is itself HISTORICAL/superseded). So the true gap is as much a governance-recognition gap (nothing currently anchors Authority under the live constitution) as a code gap.

Because none of this exists live today (only inert type definitions and a rubber-stamp validator), adopting it is effectively adopting a new, previously-unenforced core artifact family into the kernel, not merely renaming or attribute-binding an existing one.

CAPABILITY.explanation:
CAPABILITY, as defined by the minimal semantic ("a durable ability/function distinct from any one mechanism/implementation currently providing it"), already exists as a real, tested, frozen-normative concept in this repository — not merely a similarly-named field. docs/architecture/ADR-24-26-Capability-Trust-Connector.md (Status: Accepted/Frozen) states the definition almost verbatim: "Capability beskriver vad som kan göras, inte vem som får göra det" (a Capability describes WHAT can be done, not who may do it — i.e. explicitly mechanism/authority-independent), and its invariant CAP-26-I0 ("CapabilityArtifact SHALL NOT embed trust semantics") plus CAP-26-I17 ("ConnectorArtifact SHALL NOT embed capability semantics") constitutionally separate the ability from the mechanism that provides it.

This is operationalized, not just documented: packages/mps-capability/src/contracts/CapabilityDefinition.ts (and the identical artifacts/CapabilityDefinitionArtifact.ts) define a canonical, versioned artifact (capability_key, capability_version, input/output types, required_permissions) that references a separate CanonicalImplementationArtifact (packages/mps-capability/src/contracts/CanonicalImplementationArtifact.ts: runtime_hash, entrypoint, environment_constraints) via implementation_ref — the exact ability/mechanism split the candidate describes. This split is proven under test, not aspirational: packages/mps-compliance/package24/CAP.test.ts CAP-001 shows capability identity hash is stable independent of capability_key/capability_version naming; CAP-004 shows replay-deterministic execution (packages/mps-capability/src/executor/DeterministicCapabilityExecutor.ts); CAP-005 (packages/mps-capability/src/validation/DefaultImplementationReferenceValidator.ts) explicitly validates that a capability's implementation_ref matches a distinct implementation artifact, i.e. that the ability survives an implementation swap as long as the reference is re-pointed. packages/mps-capability/src/resolver/CapabilityResolver.ts's discoverByKey(capabilityKey): CapabilityDefinition[] returns a plural result, i.e. the platform already recognizes multiple definitions (potentially multiple implementations) as instances of the "same" logical capability via capability_key. packages/mps-capability-registry (CapabilityRegistryArtifact: availability "AVAILABLE"|"DEPRECATED", RegistryEngine.registerCapability/deprecateCapability) tracks capability lifecycle/availability, again keyed by (capability_ref, implementation_ref) rather than by implementation identity alone.

The lossless-reuse test does not pass with zero loss, however (see below): (a) the ADR-24-26 governance/certification/policy/trust-anchor layer (CapabilityCertificationArtifact, CapabilityPolicyArtifact, CapabilityTrustAnchorArtifact, ConnectorArtifact, EndpointArtifact) is fully specified in the frozen ADR but has NO implementing TypeScript anywhere in packages/ (grep across packages/ found zero hits for these four type names outside the ADR); only the much thinner packages/mps-runtime/src/execution/CapabilityResolutionArtifact.ts (capability_ref + actor_ref + resolution_context) exists in code, used by RuntimeAdmissionKernel.ts to check "Capability Grant closure." (b) CapabilityRegistryArtifact's availability field is scoped per (capability_ref, implementation_ref) pair, so there is no single, implementation-independent "is this capability healthy" signal today — swapping the providing implementation does not automatically preserve or aggregate availability state. (c) No file in packages/mps-decision-governance (the repo's actual "Decision" domain, concerned with DecisionImpactArtifact/EvidenceSetArtifact for environmental/legal decisions) references capability at all — so "what capability was at stake in a Decision" is not answerable from any existing cross-reference; it is answerable only at the execution/action level via CapabilityExecutionArtifact.capability_ref. I judge (c) as expected integration debt rather than evidence the concept itself is missing, since no GAO-kernel Decision/Mission/Authority/Outcome unification exists yet anywhere in this repo for ANY candidate to already be wired into (packages/mps-evolution/src/core/types.ts's ArtifactType union, which is where CAPABILITY_DEFINITION/CAPABILITY_EXECUTION/CAPABILITY_REGISTRY_ENTRY live, contains no MISSION/AUTHORITY/bare-DECISION/OUTCOME types at all). I judge (a) and (b) as real, but narrowly-scoped, attribute/relation-level gaps on an otherwise-existing concept, not proof of absence.

Separately and importantly: the repository has a SECOND, non-unified "Capability" family with materially different semantics — packages/mps-governance/src/capabilities/{CapabilityArtifact,CapabilityGrantArtifact,CapabilityScopeArtifact}.ts define Capability as "a named capability that may be granted to actors" (artifact_type "capability", lower-case, built on ArtifactContract rather than CanonicalArtifact) and CapabilityGrantArtifact as an "Immutable authorization binding" of actor+capability+scope. This is an RBAC/entitlement concept (who is allowed to invoke something), not "an ability distinct from mechanism" — it is closer to the semantic territory of the sibling AUTHORITY candidate than to CAPABILITY as minimally defined here. packages/mps-runtime/src/execution/CapabilityResolutionArtifact.ts and packages/mps-compliance's CAP_26_I1/I2/I3/I5 validators sit in this second cluster. This is a genuine naming collision inside the current codebase (two incompatible type systems both called "Capability") that a kernel freeze must resolve, independent of whether CAPABILITY itself needs a new core representation — flagged as a secondary SEMANTIC_DUPLICATE-shaped concern, not the primary finding.

Given the weight of evidence — a frozen ADR, a dedicated package with full identity/versioning/replay/registry machinery, and a passing compliance test suite that specifically proves mechanism-independence (CAP-004, CAP-005) — I conclude the core semantic already exists and does not need a new independent core artifact family. I deviate from a strict mechanical "one failing governance question forces a fall-through to CORE_SEMANTIC_SURVIVES" reading: the failing/partial questions (ADR-specified-but-unbuilt certification/policy/trust layer; per-pair rather than aggregate availability; no cross-reference from the unrelated Decision-governance domain) are addressable as NEW_DURABLE_RELATION / NEW_NORMATIVE_ATTRIBUTE work on the existing CapabilityDefinitionArtifact/CapabilityRegistryArtifact family, which the audit's own delta-categorization rules anticipate as compatible with a LATENT_REUSE finding.

CAPABILITY.minimum_semantic_delta: No new core artifact type is required. The minimum delta is: (1) a new durable relation/reference from whatever artifact ultimately represents a governed 'Decision' or 'Mission' in the future GAO kernel to the existing CapabilityDefinitionArtifact/CapabilityResolutionArtifact (today no such cross-reference exists anywhere in the codebase); (2) a new normative attribute providing an aggregate, implementation-independent availability/health rollup at the capability_key level, since CapabilityRegistryArtifact.availability today is scoped per (capability_ref, implementation_ref) pair only; and (3) resolving the naming collision between this Capability (mps-capability: ability distinct from mechanism) and the differently-scoped Capability in packages/mps-governance/src/capabilities (grantable permission/entitlement), and completing or explicitly deferring the ADR-24-26 certification/policy/trust-anchor layer that is frozen in the ADR but has no implementing code today.
semantic_conflicts: Internal naming collision: packages/mps-capability (+ mps-capability-registry) models Capability as an ability distinct from its implementation (matches this candidate's minimal definition), while packages/mps-governance/src/capabilities/* independently models Capability as a grantable, actor-scoped permission/entitlement (artifact_type 'capability', built on a different base type ArtifactContract vs CanonicalArtifact) — these are two non-unified representations sharing one name.

The mps-governance CapabilityGrantArtifact/CapabilityScopeArtifact semantics ('who may exercise what, in what scope') look more like they belong under the sibling AUTHORITY candidate than under CAPABILITY as minimally defined for this audit; flagging for the AUTHORITY reviewer's awareness.

DECISION.explanation:
DECISION was tested in order against the repository's actual constitutional documents and TypeScript contracts, not just against similarly-named types.

(1) WRONG_ABSTRACTION_LEVEL rejected: the platform already treats "decision" as a load-bearing normative boundary, not an implementation concern. ADR-24-21 (Actor-Identity-Trust, constitutional) ACT-21-I10 requires "Any governance decision requiring mutation authority SHALL reference exactly one AuthorityEvidenceArtifact," and packages/mps-registry/src/contracts/RegistryMutationArtifacts.ts:9-10 hard-gates state mutation on a `promotion_decision_ref` (REG-24-13-I1: "Registry SHALL NOT mutate state without a valid PromotionDecisionArtifact reference"). This is core governance plumbing, not UI/logging/backend-swap material.

(2) MECHANISM_ONLY rejected: packages/mps-governance/src/engine/GovernancePolicyEngine.ts:56-85 shows the *output* of decision logic (`governance_result`, `decided_by`, `rationale`) is itself the governed artifact, not a description of how a vote was computed. ADR-MPS-CORE-001.md:180-186 explicitly forbids re-deriving a Decision from a stale Category-C derived value, treating Decision as a distinct, non-recomputable normative fact, not a mechanism detail.

(3) ALREADY_REPRESENTED — tested via the Lossless Semantic Reuse Test below — FAILS. (4) SEMANTIC_DUPLICATE — the existing decision-shaped artifacts are not identical to each other (see schema drift below), so this class does not cleanly apply either; noted as a secondary finding. (5) DERIVABLE rejected: ADR-MPS-CORE-001.md's Trust Boundary Recalculation Rule (§5.2) explicitly forbids reusing a recomputed derived value as authorization for a new decision ("Old FitnessScore → [forbidden] → New PromotionDecision"), and EXEC-25-I3 (ADR-24-25) requires Attempt/Decision immutability after publication — i.e. the platform's own constitution requires a decision to be explicitly, immutably recorded at decision time, not reconstructed from Evidence+Outcome after the fact. (6) NOT_TECHNOLOGY_INDEPENDENT rejected: "who chose what, when, under what authority" survives any swap of the underlying selection mechanism (human review, deterministic policy engine, or an LLM), matching EXEC-25-I15 Runtime Independence already asserted for the adjacent Execution model. (7) NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_GOVERNED rejected: the concept is *already* independently instantiated as its own top-level `CanonicalArtifact` (own content_hash/identity, own artifact_type tag) in at least four separate packages (mps-core's trust-boundary example, mps-evolution, mps-promotion, mps-governance) rather than being folded as a field onto Evidence or Outcome artifacts — convergent, repeated, independent re-invention of the same shape is itself evidence that the concept needs its own lifecycle, not that it is derivable from something else's.

Having survived 1-7, disposition reaches (8) CORE_SEMANTIC_SURVIVES / TRUE_GAP — but this is a normalization-flavored true gap, not a from-nothing one: docs/architecture/AI-GOVERNANCE-AND-HUMAN-AUTHORITY-01.md is the repository's own first-party admission of exactly this gap. §2 states the constitutional rule ("FINAL DECISION AUTHORITY = an explicitly identified, authorized human actor... on the artifact that constitutes the decision") and its own Gap paragraph (lines 73-79) says: "no artifact type in this codebase is yet explicitly named or typed as a legal/administrative decision subject to this rule... The mechanisms above govern governance actions on data (import, promotion, source approval), not yet an end-user-facing decision artifact." §3 independently names "observation → interpretation → decision" as an existing conceptual separation ("GENERATED != DECISION," line 98) that has never been reified as its own canonical artifact family. §9's AI-GOV-3 explicitly calls for "Decision-subject artifact typing... distinct from governance actions on data" as a still-open, unscheduled item. This is a documented, self-identified TRUE_GAP, corroborated independently by the code-level drift found below.

DECISION.minimum_semantic_delta: A single, kernel-owned, canonically-versioned Decision artifact family (analogous in rigor to how mps-decision-governance owns the `dg-*` namespace for DecisionImpact identity) that: (1) references the full set of identifiable alternatives considered, not merely the one candidate that was chosen -- a field that exists nowhere in the repository today; (2) makes the authority binding (an ActorReference / AuthorityEvidenceArtifact reference) and the point-in-time timestamp mandatory, non-optional fields on every instance, closing the drift between the mps-promotion and mps-evolution variants; (3) references, but stays structurally distinct from, the evidence/evaluation material considered beforehand and the Outcome artifact that follows, per the separation already asserted informally in ADR-24-25 and AI-GOVERNANCE-AND-HUMAN-AUTHORITY-01.md §3 ('GENERATED != DECISION'); (4) is immutable after publication and independently content-addressed, so it can supersede -- rather than sit alongside -- the currently-duplicated PROMOTION_DECISION / PROMOTION_DECISION_ARTIFACT / GOVERNANCE_APPROVAL / GOVERNANCE_APPROVAL_ARTIFACT artifact_type variants as their common canonical ancestor. EVIDENCE.explanation: EVIDENCE ("material that supports or documents a claim about a past/present state of affairs, distinct from interpretation/conclusion") is not an unrepresented semantic in this repository — it is already a mature, constitutionally-frozen concept, but it exists as at least three independently-evolved artifact families in three different domains rather than one unified kernel type: (1) EvidenceSetArtifact in mps-decision-governance (content-addressed, lineage-DAG-governed sets of document refs feeding DecisionImpact, named "Raw Evidence" in the platform's own constitution), (2) DocumentEvidenceArtifact + DocumentFactCore/source_span in mps-lu/mps-data-governance (LU-domain evidentiary binding with a compiler-enforced CANDIDATE/VERIFIED split), and (3) EvidenceBundle/RankedEvidence/LegalEvidence in mps-lu's retrieval layer (RAG citation evidence with SUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED/INSUFFICIENT relation to a claim). All three independently satisfy the candidate's own governance-question set (traceable origin via content_hash, structural separation from interpretation, decision reconstructability, tamper/unreliability detection) using the same shared kernel primitives already in mps-core (CanonicalArtifact, ContentReference, HashDescriptor, ActorReference). Because the semantics is expressed multiple times, independently, by domain-owned artifact families built on shared generic primitives — rather than needing a wholly new kernel artifact type — this falls under SEMANTIC_DUPLICATE rather than a clean single ALREADY_REPRESENTED, and rather than CORE_SEMANTIC_SURVIVES. A future "Governed Autonomous Operations" capability's evidence need is very likely satisfiable the same way its predecessors were: by instantiating a domain-scoped evidence artifact on top of ContentReference/CanonicalArtifact plus a mandatory-source-span-style binding, not by minting a new top-level EVIDENCE core type. The residual gap, if any, is a cross-domain normative contract/interface that makes the repeated pattern explicit and reusable, not new semantics.

A hypothetical fourth domain (Governed Autonomous Operations) could not point at one of these and get full coverage without loss -- it would have to build its own instance of the same pattern, as every prior domain did. This is why the overall test is marked FAIL at the 'single representation' bar even though every individual governance question is answerable within any one existing domain's own representation.

EVIDENCE.minimum_semantic_delta: Not a new EVIDENCE artifact type. If anything is missing, it is a thin cross-domain normative contract/interface (built on the existing mps-core primitives: ContentReference, CanonicalArtifact, ActorReference) that makes explicit the pattern every existing evidence family already independently implements — mandatory content-addressed source binding, structural separation from any interpretation/conclusion type, and referenceability from a decision-like artifact's own identity — so a new domain (e.g. Governed Autonomous Operations) can conform to it instead of re-deriving the pattern from scratch a fourth time. This is a contract-level normalization across existing/future domains, not a new durable kernel type, new relation, or new field on a currently-existing type.
semantic_conflicts: Possible naming collision with a 'DECISION' kernel candidate: this repo's own constitution already uses 'Decision Truth' / DecisionImpactArtifact as the interpretive layer that Evidence feeds into (ADR-MPS-CONSTITUTIONAL-INVARIANTS.md §3) — any new kernel DECISION concept should be checked against DecisionImpactArtifact for the same kind of duplication found here for EVIDENCE.

The mps-data-governance DocumentFactArtifact sits ambiguously between 'evidence' and 'decision/interpretation' in its own domain (its header explicitly calls itself Tier 3 classification, i.e. interpretation, yet its source_span is evidentiary) — a kernel-level EVIDENCE/DECISION split should account for this existing domain's own layering (Tier 2 content -> Tier 3 fact -> Governance verification -> LU evidence -> LU rule) rather than assuming a clean two-way split.

MISSION.explanation:
MISSION is defined as "the reason a system-level course of action is undertaken." Searching the whole repository (docs/architecture, packages/, server/) turns up zero uses of "Mission" as an architectural term (only one unrelated colloquial hit: docs/ops/agent-instructions/TOR_INSTRUKTION_JURIDISK_RAG_IMPLEMENTATION.md:19, "Din mission" = "your assignment," not a domain concept). So there is no naming collision to worry about, and the question is purely semantic: does anything in the frozen kernel need to carry "why was this course of action undertaken, who authorized that purpose, and is it still valid"?

The platform has, twice, independently confronted exactly this "why" semantic, and both times deliberately kept it OUT of the CanonicalArtifact-based normative decision kernel that ADR-MPS-CORE-001 / ADR-MPS-CONSTITUTIONAL-INVARIANTS.md governs:

1. System/application-level purpose is expressed as an ADR/"Charter" (docs/architecture/ADR-27-LU-Architecture-Charter.md:1-16, "## 0. Syfte" / "Detta dokument är bindande för all utveckling av LU v1.0"). This is a human-authored, git-versioned prose document reviewed through the ADR process — not a runtime CanonicalArtifact with hash identity, signature, or an ActorReference-based authorization chain like every other kernel artifact (ADR-24-21/22). Its "authority" is document governance, not artifact governance.

2. Engagement/analysis-level purpose is expressed as `LUProjectContextArtifact` (docs/architecture/LU-v1.0-Project-Context.md:1-40): fields `project_description`, `activity_description`, `planned_activity` are literally "the reason work occurs" for an LU engagement. Critically, the architects wrote explicit invariants excluding it from governance: "Den är inte en del av governance." / "Den får aldrig påverka governance." / "Ny regel: Project Context is not truth." This is direct first-party evidence that when this exact semantic (why is this work happening) arose, the designers chose to keep it as inert, non-authoritative domain payload rather than a governance-gating kernel concept — precisely the role MISSION's own governance questions (Q3 scope-compliance, Q5 validity-at-decision-time) would require it to play.

This is reinforced by the kernel's own frozen, exhaustive decision-input chain: ADR-MPS-CORE-001 §8 states governance "får endast fatta beslut baserat på: CanonicalArtifact → Verified Reference → Verified Evidence → Recomputed Metrics → Decision Artifact," explicitly forbidding "Caller supplied score, Unverified reference, Cached fitness." Nothing resembling an externally asserted "purpose/objective" is in that enumerated chain in either of the two forms purpose currently takes on this platform. Elevating MISSION to a gating, authority-checked kernel concept would require rewriting this frozen constitutional chain, which is itself the signal that the concept — as the candidate defines it — sits at the ADR/document-governance layer or the non-authoritative domain-context layer, not the artifact kernel.

Secondary observations supporting the same conclusion: PolicyArtifact/PolicyScope (packages/mps-governance/src/contracts/PolicyArtifact.ts:4-15) and GovernanceRule (packages/mps-governance/src/types.ts:13-18) express WHAT rules/conditions must hold (a procedural constraint gate — closer to MECHANISM_ONLY territory), never WHY the work exists. CapabilityScopeArtifact/CapabilityGrantArtifact (packages/mps-governance/src/capabilities/*.ts) express the scope of an AUTHORIZATION to execute a capability, not an organizational objective. GovernanceApprovalArtifact.rationale (packages/mps-governance/src/artifacts/GovernanceApprovalArtifact.ts:11) is free text tied 1:1 to a single approval event with no independent identity, versioning, or issuing authority of its own. EvolutionPolicy (packages/mps-evolution/src/EvolutionPolicy.ts) — the closest thing to an "autonomous operation" governor already in the codebase — is purely threshold-based (quality gain, mutation ratio) with no objective/goal field at all. None of these compete with MISSION as reuse candidates; they simply confirm no existing kernel artifact carries this semantic, while the two places that do carry it (Charter, ProjectContext) are both explicitly non-kernel by design.

I therefore rule this WRONG_ABSTRACTION_LEVEL rather than CORE_SEMANTIC_SURVIVES: the semantics are real (the platform demonstrably needs to express "why," and has built two different non-kernel mechanisms to do so), but the platform's own architects, when they hit this exact question, twice chose a layer other than the normative artifact-governance kernel this audit is testing candidates for.

OUTCOME.explanation:
The platform already has a frozen, independently governed, actively-implemented "Outcome" concept — ExecutionOutcome / FrozenExecutionOutcomeIdentity — that matches the candidate's minimal definition closely enough that minting a new core type for OUTCOME would duplicate existing normative machinery rather than fill a gap.

ADR-24-25 (Execution Identity & Attempt Model) defines "Execution Outcome" explicitly as "Canonical representation av resultatet" (SUCCESS | FAILURE | PARTIAL | CANCELLED | UNKNOWN) that is produced from exactly one ExecutionAttemptArtifact (the "action"), is bound to that attempt via a mandatory reference (EXEC-25-I7: "ExecutionAttemptArtifact SHALL reference exactly one ExecutionOutcomeArtifact"), and is subsequently consumed as decision evidence by governance (EXEC-25-I11: "PromotionDecisionArtifact SHALL reference the ExecutionOutcomeArtifact ... used as decision evidence"). ADR-29 froze this identity into the runtime as part of "Runtime Contract Freeze (v1.0.0)" and made ExecutionKernel "the only client-facing motor API" that all domain packages (present and future) must go through — meaning any future Governed-Autonomous-Operations domain, per the platform's own architecture, would be structurally required to route its actions through ExecutionKernel and would therefore already receive ExecutionOutcome artifacts for its attempts rather than needing a parallel concept.

In code this is not aspirational: packages/mps-runtime/src/contracts/freeze/FrozenIdentities.ts implements FrozenExecutionOutcomeIdentityV1/V2 with a canonical content-hash body, a fail-closed validateFrozenExecutionOutcomeIdentity (rejects tampered attempt/capability-execution refs), and an explicit contract-version lifecycle (V1 historical, V2 self-validating) — i.e. it already has independent governance/versioning of its own (satisfying governance Q5). packages/mps-runtime/src/unit/FrozenExecutionOutcomeSelfConsistency.test.ts proves self-rehash, non-aliasing, and fail-closed tamper rejection. packages/mps-runtime/src/kernel/ExecutionKernel.ts wires a first-class "outcome" node into the runtime execution graph (RuntimeState.ts:20, kind "capability" | "workflow_step" | "outcome"), and packages/mps-runtime/src/contracts/model/ExecutionContracts.ts gives ExecutionSession an outcome_ref alongside its manifest/ticket/attempt/replay refs — so outcomes are durably, canonically bound into the same reference graph as the action that produced them (governance Q4 — traceable to the producing attempt).

The architecture also already structurally separates the neutral "what happened" record from the classified result: ADR-24-25 defines a distinct ObservedExecutionGraphArtifact ("Canonical projektion av exekveringsresultatet") alongside ExecutionOutcomeArtifact — i.e. the "state of affairs" observation and the outcome classification are already two separate, cross-referenced artifact types (partially satisfying governance Q3; the classification (success/failure) is itself a technical determination, not yet a real-world "goodness" evaluation layer, but that gap is a downstream DECISION/EVIDENCE-layer concern, not evidence that Outcome itself is missing).

Comparison against "what was expected/intended beforehand" (governance Q2) is not a single first-class field on ExecutionOutcomeArtifact, but is fully reconstructible without semantic loss by joining the existing, already-linked ExecutionManifestArtifact (the canonical record of intent: inputs/configuration/policies, ADR-24-25 "Execution Manifest") against ExecutionOutcome + ObservedExecutionGraph via the attempt_ref/manifest_ref chain that EXEC-25-I20 and I7 already mandate. This is DERIVABLE-strength reuse, not a gap requiring new normative structure.

I examined other repository representations carrying the word "outcome" and rejected them as distinct or mechanism-only: MaterializationOutcome (packages/mps-decision-governance/src/MaterializationContract.ts:47-61) is a pipeline call's return-shape (REUSED|CREATED with steps) — it describes HOW a materialization pipeline ran, not a normative resulting state of a decision/action, and is not an artifact type at all (MECHANISM_ONLY, rejected as reuse candidate, noted as a naming collision risk only). DecisionImpactIdentity/Artifact (packages/mps-decision-governance/src/DecisionImpactIdentity.ts:30-67) is an aggregated statistical indicator materialized across many source decisions (e.g. permit counts per jurisdiction/period) — a population-level metric, not the resulting state of one specific decision/action, so it does not carry OUTCOME's per-action semantics. ExecutionTicketStatus (pending/leased/running/completed/failed/retry, FrozenIdentities.ts:176-190) is queue/scheduling mechanism state, not a normative resulting state of affairs.

I found no top-level constitutional treatment of "Outcome": ADR-MPS-CONSTITUTIONAL-INVARIANTS.md and ADR-MPS-CORE-001.md contain no mention of it — the concept is governed one layer down, at ADR-24-25/ADR-29, which is the active, README-indexed (section 3, "Active domain / TV contracts", README.md:74-75) authority for it. That is enough independent, non-superseded governance to ground reuse (ADR-24-20, the old Package-24 constitution, is explicitly marked superseded/NORMATIVE_TODAY:false in README.md:20-23, but ADR-29 — which freezes exactly the Execution Outcome identity ADR-24-25 defines — is not superseded and is still listed as active).

Net: the candidate's core semantics (a resulting state, produced by and traceable to a specific action, distinct in record from the intent that preceded it, independently versioned/governed) already exist, are frozen, are tested for fail-closed integrity, and are architecturally mandatory for any new domain (including a future GAO capability) to reuse rather than reinvent. Confidence is STRONG rather than PROVEN because the "compare against intent" and "goodness judgment" aspects require joining across artifacts rather than a single field, and because a GAO capability's real-world (non-execution-technical) consequence tracking is not yet demonstrated end-to-end in this repository — but nothing in that gap requires a new core artifact family; it composes on what already exists.

OUTCOME.minimum_semantic_delta: No new core artifact family, contract, relation, or attribute is required to serve the candidate's stated semantics. The existing chain ExecutionManifest(intent) → ExecutionAttempt(action) → ExecutionOutcome + ObservedExecutionGraph(result), already mandatorily bound by EXEC-25-I7/I11/I20 and mandatorily reused by any domain client under ADR-29's single-motor-API rule, already answers the material governance questions. If a future Governed-Autonomous-Operations capability needs domain-specific (non-execution-technical) consequence tracking — e.g. an environmental/regulatory effect beyond 'did the code run successfully' — that would be a downstream attribute or artifact hung off outcome_ref/attempt_ref within the existing reference-closure model (at most a NEW_NORMATIVE_ATTRIBUTE later, not a new independently-governed core type), and is not established as a proven need by anything found in this repository today.
negative_findings: No mention of 'outcome' anywhere in ADR-MPS-CONSTITUTIONAL-INVARIANTS.md or ADR-MPS-CORE-001.md — the concept is governed one layer down (ADR-24-25/ADR-29), not at the top constitutional layer.

ExecutionOutcomeArtifact carries no explicit 'expected/intended' field to diff against — the expected-vs-actual comparison is derivable via a join across ExecutionManifest + ExecutionOutcome/ObservedExecutionGraph, not a single first-class field.

No demonstrated end-to-end example in this repository of a domain-specific, non-execution-technical (e.g. real-world environmental/regulatory) consequence being recorded as an 'outcome' distinct from code-execution success/failure — the gap, if any, is at that higher evaluative layer, not at the core Outcome representation.

PromotionDecisionArtifact — the concept that consumes ExecutionOutcome as decision evidence — is independently redefined in at least 4 separate files across 3 packages (mps-governance, mps-evolution, mps-promotion), a duplication risk relevant to the DECISION candidate, not OUTCOME.
semantic_conflicts: MaterializationOutcome (packages/mps-decision-governance/src/MaterializationContract.ts:47) and MaterializationOutcome usage in MaterializationPipeline.ts share the 'Outcome' name with the candidate but describe an unrelated, mechanism-level pipeline return type — a naming collision, not a semantic duplicate, worth flagging so a future kernel does not conflate the two.

PromotionDecisionArtifact is defined independently in packages/mps-governance/src/engine/GovernancePolicyEngine.ts, packages/mps-evolution/src/governance/PromotionDecisionArtifact.ts, and twice in packages/mps-promotion/src/contracts/ — a same-name, multiply-defined type that is the primary consumer of ExecutionOutcome as decision evidence; flagged for the DECISION candidate's own audit as a possible SEMANTIC_DUPLICATE, not resolved here.
